description: The complete public coverage boundary of loopmmt.com: one node per served public leaf, typed by coverage class. This is the reader's coverage oracle for a full excavation (see The Reckoning). It is a pure fold over the same tree the sitemap walks — nodes[].url equals sitemap.xml's <loc> set, independently checkable. It enumerates the public boundary, not the private canon: what is redacted or private is absent from the served tree and therefore absent here.
coverage_note: core = read for a Reconnaissance pass; standard = mid-tier content, read in full excavation; deep = evidentiary leaves (prompts), full excavation only; optional = supporting tools / app docs. A complete excavation reads every core+standard+deep node, or declares each skipped node optional/inaccessible by name. 'Everything' means every node here examined or explicitly accounted for — not that all of Loop MMT is public (25/307 KPs are published; the methodology generator is private by design).

nodes.title: Loop MMT
nodes.description: An antifragile cognitive operating system that uses both AI and determinism as its processor and git as its state and store. Made from a one-room RV in Maine.

nodes.title: A Loop MMT Language · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A programming language for Loop MMT — write a program in the method's own terms, save it as a file, call it later, and pipe one program into another like functions. The brief includes a sketched program that runs a Kaleidoscope, drafts a plan, revises through Parallax and a Red Team teardown, and presents for download.

nodes.title: Bring All Boats To Level · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Email, calendar, and contacts drifted apart as they were built separately. Build a process (not the work) that reads N apps' design and capabilities, finds where a color scheme or drag pattern from one belongs in the others, and brings all boats to the same level — folded into the Work Hierarchy, gated, deterministic where scripts can do it, ending in a well-defined Block^N work plan.

nodes.title: DDE Stitch Into The Whole System · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A question routed through a fully-composed session: how can the DDE protocol Stitch into the whole system? The deliverable is a plan for doing exactly that.

nodes.title: Do It — AX · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: The go-ahead that turned the Red Team brief into a build. Having laid out the whole design in the prior prompt, the operator closes the loop with the shortest possible instruction.

nodes.title: Ecosystem Master-View · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: The Loop World app collection is approaching seventy, and there's no top-down way to manage it. The ask is a framework and a Master View — stats, monitoring, and protocolized dev actions across the whole constellation.

nodes.title: Email Design System · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Not how the email app will look — how the DESIGN SYSTEM for it will look. Pan Gmail's patterns for gold, then build the system up from there, block by block.

nodes.title: Come Up With An Entirely Novel Way To Develop Software · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: The prompt that named the whole methodology — an unbounded re-think-everything mandate anchored to one falsifiable proof: a three-day butcher-shop app.

nodes.title: Every File To Git · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Redesign how the system works with files. Files live in two places with no clear standard; the operator wants drastically fewer files to touch — never to manage session-state files or remember a registry again — and one new posture: every file gets saved to git, in a smart structure.

nodes.title: Field As A Moving Map · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: The prompt reframes a familiar metric as a field. Once “how far from the goal” becomes “how hard is each point on the map,” a scalar turns into a topology — and the interesting question becomes the path, not the position.

nodes.title: Formalize A Gate · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Gates are used all over the system, well, and are explained in the Glossary — but the abstract concept of what a gate is had never been written down in one place. Define, design, and build that idea, in a way that makes gates better: more general, better-connected to reporting and logging. And a real challenge — can you inject a little sparkle, whimsy and chaos, into something as mundane as a gate spec, without discoloring results?

nodes.title: Full Knowledge Map Of All Things · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A pre-built map of all knowledge that a system then fills in — throw out the ad-hoc KP graph, start from the atoms of everything humans have learned, build them into right-sized blocks, and assemble the blocks into a map whose empty cells name the next KPs to make.

nodes.title: Hex → Three Rules · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A distillation is its own kind of engineering. “Three rules a seven-year-old can follow” is a compression spec with a hard fidelity constraint — the rules have to still generate the real offense.

nodes.title: How This Site Is Made · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Fully dogfood: design a new system and a page on how this website is being made — look back over the development arc, decide what a “how it's made” page should even be, back-fill it from the real records, and keep a log so it stays current. Derived rather than traditionally logged — a ledger with pointers — and formalized into a reusable system, using the two-audience format (prose for humans, dense distillate for AI, in one document).

nodes.title: Image-as-Framing-Lens · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A framing step where the instance examines real images (fractals, and oddly, the prompt to think about grocery stores) as a lens on a problem — generalized so any image can be a default frame in a framing deliberation.

nodes.title: Jukebox Protocol · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A quick idea, dropped mid-build: a Jukebox Protocol that would let the AI hear music better — a Context Mesh per song, organized like a record collection.

nodes.title: Loop Generalized Language · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: In the Loop 2.1 computer, the operator built keyboard shortcuts for himself. This prompt wants the same idea here — a code-like language for driving the methodology.

nodes.title: Make Sure All The Little Details Sparkle · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: The maximal operator prompt — a full build commission with its own process scaffold baked in, and the whole quality drive in one sentence.

nodes.title: A Map Of The Equations To The Places They Show Up · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: The operator's own theory of how you think, handed back as a build spec: math as navigable shape-space, and a tool to move through it.

nodes.title: One Shape, Wide Latitude · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A planning-only experiment: seed a whole run with almost nothing — one green lattice shape — throw the full Programs suite at it (every Plane, then the Gauntlet), and let the model fold the shape into the work however it can.

nodes.title: Pan For Gold · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A pan is casting wide for the analogy that cracks a problem, then compressing hard. The unrelated topics aren't noise — they're the search space, chosen for distance because distance is where the non-obvious structure lives.

nodes.title: Park-It-As-Debt · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A move the operator just made — hit an unsolvable, decided to park it, wrote it down as debt, and kept going — examined for whether it deserves to be a formal protocol.

nodes.title: If You Shrute It, You Glorp It · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A prompt that edits the system's own vocabulary mid-flight — coining a term, wiring it to a real correction mechanism, and catching a packaging defect in the same breath.

nodes.title: Super Frame → Triple Random → Gold Bar · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Naming the topics biases the search; leaving them random doesn't. This specimen trusts the collision, not the curator — the operator declines to pre-decide what will turn out to be relevant.

nodes.title: The Best Loading Path · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Could the site be better at how an AI takes in the whole thing? We give AI all the tools and materials to parse, understand, and report on Loop MMT — but we don't explicitly tell it how. Not to control its framing: to help other systems get their head around the whole thing the way the system understands itself. What's the best loading path for an AI to absorb this corpus — and, generalized, the best loading path for anything to understand anything?

nodes.title: The Climber-Coder · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A new Dev Crew member: an old-school Yosemite dirtbag climber who also, quietly, cranked bits for an early tech company and left something load-bearing under the modern world — casual about the code, obsessive about the beauty of a line on rock, a world-class fiddle player, kind, weird, well-off under the affect.

nodes.title: The Deployment System · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A deploy bottleneck named precisely: parallel sessions have to wait on each other because each one runs its own deployment. The ask is a shared system that batches their work instead.

nodes.title: The Discovery Invocation · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Some prompts are tuning forks, not tasks. This one sets the key — the discovery register plus the autonomy contract — and leaves the actual build to whatever runs inside it next.

nodes.title: The Elegance Check · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A pass that can be called at any point to force a brutally clear look at whatever is in front of the room, cutting what doesn't need to be there — subtractive, but never subtraction for its own sake.

nodes.title: The Ferry Audit · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: With the Ferry — the system for applying Loop MMT protocols to software — freshly built, run a broad audit across loopmmt.com and the Forest app for the most interesting, most positively-impactful protocol (or chain or tree of protocols) that could be Ferried onto them. Focus sharply on pragmatic, buildable-now things that make the site run better, more efficiently, or with new capabilities. No target count — find the best ones to start, and think weird.

nodes.title: The Forest Punch List · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Assemble everything the Forest needs done — everything this line turned up — onto the Punch List, then start working it. Plan smartly, think in blocks, and bake in mechanisms that use all available context: do the fruitful work that fits in a session, fill the Cistern at the end with spare drops, run a good handoff, and pick up on a fresh tank. Rinse and repeat.

nodes.title: The Grab Feedback · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Drag-and-drop is snappy but doesn't feel like anything — click and the cursor stays a cursor, release and the item just appears. Look at it through the human point of view (and the UI knowledge) and find the affordance that makes a drag feel like holding something.

nodes.title: The Highest Derivative · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: “The highest derivative” is a method, not a topic: keep taking the derivative of the idea — refine the refinement — until you reach the most general form that still holds.

nodes.title: The Longest Short Story · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Sometimes the prompt is a tuning fork. It sets a resonance and then asks for work in that key, not about it.

nodes.title: The Minecart Traffic-Circle · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A minecart contraption in Minecraft — a traffic circle where a cart loops forever until the player reverses, and when you reverse determines which line you exit — gave the operator one of those “there's SOMETHING here” feelings. Take in the transcript and image but explicitly don't anchor on any of ChatGPT's solutions — use them only as jumping-off points — and parallax your own design: deterministic to the spine, with the time component worked in, aimed at a control structure usable in the method or (via the Ferry) in the software.

nodes.title: The Namespace Collision · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A system that has set aside dozens of ordinary words to mean specific things needs a guard against reusing one of those words in its plain sense — a collision inside its own documents. Fold that check into how the system operates.

nodes.title: The Non-Caring Protocol · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A delegation rule stated as a feeling: when the operator has no stake in how a task is done — only that it gets done — the system should decide and proceed without a fork back, provided doing so is safe.

nodes.title: The Red Team · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: An adversarial crew of five-to-seven AI specialists from outside the board, each as developed as a board member, built to break, poke holes, and find gaps — and, in person, the most charming people you'll ever meet.

nodes.title: The Undo-Send · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: The thirty-second send countdown traps the user in the compose window. Instead: hit send, optionally confirm, close the window, show a sent notice, and fade an undo-send button into the bottom-left with a thirty-second timer (numeric + visual). Undo reopens the email exactly as it was; let it lapse and the button quietly disappears.

nodes.title: The Word Square · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A word square that reads the same across and down — do these scale up with processes or ideas? What if each square were one of the system's blocks? Build into the empty space rather than chipping to find a shape; find the simplest thing that is still real, buildable, and powerful.

nodes.title: Tune The Concurrency System · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: Pause and look at the concurrency system six weeks in — read all the session history for where friction persists, ask how the newer Chain, Story Pole, and Projects systems roll in, and FBD the recurring problems out of existence rather than solving them as they pop up. Brutally lightweight, riding the Simplicity Yield.

nodes.title: Ultimate Frisbee 5-Week Curriculum · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A five-week, three-tier ultimate frisbee curriculum for kids in grades 2–8 (2/3, 4/5, 6/7/8), Mondays and Wednesdays, 45 working minutes after a 15-minute warm-up, built around throwing and catching over complicated drills.

nodes.title: Verify Real Cheaply · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: “Don't trust, verify” is good — but could you verify REAL cheaply? Spend twenty minutes learning Fact X that implies Fact Y; later, when the system meets Fact Y, confirm it in two seconds rather than twenty, with provenance (X → Y) on request. When to save something as verified, when to ask. Something to do with hashes?

nodes.title: What A Dog Needs To Know · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: A Knowledge Pack for what a dog needs to know — grounded in science and reality like the cat. But a dog isn't a cat: breeds differ enough to need two composing layers (base Dog + specific Border Collie), and maybe a shared substrate for what any animal needs.

nodes.title: What Is A Pattern · The Prompts · Loop MMT
nodes.description: The drag-and-drop — like the tabs before it — is a pattern. Is the Pattern Registry the right home, and should it split (app-build vs. internal-method)? How does the system recognize a pattern is present — what IS a pattern, defined so it can be quickly measured? And how do you build an always-check so the registry is consulted before building?

Gifts — Loop MMT
nodes.description: Four small, standalone tools pulled out of Loop MMT and given away under the MIT license. Each ships with its limits printed on it.

nodes.title: Cairn — a Loop MMT gift
nodes.description: Priority-ordered failover clone, a host-aware credential helper, and redundant push across distinct-class git stores — so your canonical history survives any one store going away. The load-bearing idea is the independence class: two mirrors on one provider aren't redundancy.

nodes.title: Census — a Loop MMT gift
nodes.description: Walk a tree, count your markers (TODO, FIXME, or whatever you define), and say which ones are buried inside comments where nobody will act on them. A report, not a gate — until you add --strict, and then a buried marker is an exit code your CI can catch.

nodes.title: Gitlog — a Loop MMT gift
nodes.description: Turn a git history into one JSON object per commit on stdout, so the questions you actually have — how many commits touched this file, who authored what last week, churn per day — become one pipe away instead of re-parsing git's text yourself. Field names match what git-log folds already read.

nodes.title: Grain — a Loop MMT gift
nodes.description: Compress your data, compare the ratio against a size-matched random null model drawn live, and get a self-calibrating reading of how much structure vs. noise — no hand-set threshold. Snapshot it over time and it becomes a cheap drift alarm.

nodes.title: Mint — a Loop MMT gift
nodes.description: Hand out IDs that are never reused — and prove it before returning each one, not with an after-the-fact check but as a structural property: a retired ID cannot come back. JSON in, JSON out, backed by a file you can read.

nodes.title: Plumb — a Loop MMT gift
nodes.description: A tiny audit pattern for anyone whose dashboards turn green on intention instead of evidence. Each claim names a witness — a file that must exist, text that must be present, a command that must pass — and only renders green if its witness agrees. Assert done with nothing beneath it and you get UNWITNESSED, not a pass.

nodes.title: Vclock — a Loop MMT gift
nodes.description: Reason about the causal order of a stream of records — is A before B, or are they concurrent, causally independent, neither able to have known about the other? Wall-clock time can't express that last case; a vector clock can. bump, merge, and compare over JSON lines, so it sits in the middle of a pipe.

nodes.title: Ward — a Loop MMT gift
nodes.description: A status badge that will not go solid on hope. Every filled cell carries a witness beneath it — a file that must exist, a file that must contain a string, or a command that must exit 0 — and renders solid only when that witness agrees right now. Any claim whose witness is missing or disagrees renders a hollow ring, never a silent solid.
